title: TensorGuard: Static Tensor Shape Verification for PyTorch

reviewers.name: Cesar Sanchez
reviewers.key_strength: The 5-theory product domain with machine-checked Tinelli-Zarba composition soundness is a genuine contribution to domain-specific SMT verification.
reviewers.key_weakness: The IC3/PDR adaptation lacks a formal interpolation completeness argument for the shape constraint domain, making the unbounded verification heuristic rather than verified.

reviewers.name: Roderick Bloem
reviewers.key_strength: Implicit specification approach with CI/CD integration (SARIF, exit codes) demonstrates deployment maturity rare in academic verification tools.
reviewers.key_weakness: No comparison with existing shape checking tools (TorchScript, mypy tensor plugins) makes it impossible to assess the marginal value of heavyweight SMT-based verification.

reviewers.name: Vasco Vasconcelos
reviewers.key_strength: The refinement type structure with IC3/PDR reframed as inductive type inference and CEGAR as principal type inference is an elegant application of type-theoretic ideas.
reviewers.key_weakness: The decidability boundary of the refinement type system is uncharacterized, and Knuth-Bendix completion cannot succeed for the full shape algebra involving nonlinear integer arithmetic.

consensus_strengths: The 5-theory product domain (Shape×Device×Phase×Stride×Permutation) with verified Nelson-Oppen/Tinelli-Zarba composition soundness is a well-designed and formally grounded contribution to domain-specific verification.
IC3/PDR unbounded verification with 9.5–21.2× speedup provides genuine safety guarantees for all symbolic dimension values, not just sampled ones.
Zero false positives on 230 benchmarks with 100% proof certificate coverage meets the soundness standard required for CI gate deployment.
Comprehensive engineering effort — 193+ operators, 6,054 tests, SARIF integration, CLI tooling, TorchBench evaluation — demonstrates practical deployment maturity.
consensus_weaknesses: The IC3/PDR adaptation to shape verification lacks formal justification: no Craig interpolation completeness argument for the shape domain, and correctness relies on empirical agreement rather than proof.
Composition soundness claims under Tinelli-Zarba are suspect for the Stride theory, which involves divisibility predicates that may violate the convexity precondition required for completeness.
The Lean 4 mechanization scope is ambiguous — it is unclear which theorems are fully mechanized versus stated as axioms, undermining the mechanization claims.
No comparison with existing shape checking tools (TorchScript, ShapeFlow, mypy/pyright tensor plugins) prevents assessment of the marginal value of SMT-based verification over simpler approaches.

The decidability boundary of the refinement type system is uncharacterized: nonlinear integer arithmetic arising from convolution formulas is undecidable, and the system may return 'unknown' for decidable instances.
actionable_recommendations: Provide a formal argument or reference that the shape constraint domain admits Craig interpolation, ensuring IC3/PDR frame refinement completeness, or clearly state that the procedure is sound but incomplete.
Clarify the Lean 4 mechanization scope by listing which theorems are fully mechanized and which are admitted, and provide the Lean source for independent verification.
Add baseline comparisons against at least 2-3 existing shape checking tools (TorchScript, mypy tensor plugins, ShapeFlow) to quantify the marginal benefit of SMT-based verification.
Characterize the decidable fragment of integer arithmetic that arises from the 193+ transfer functions and document which operators produce nonlinear constraints that may cause 'unknown' verdicts.
Provide a formal adequacy theorem relating the denotational semantics of the shape algebra to PyTorch's runtime shape computation, at least for a representative subset of operators.
